commits.edited_message:
rar5: tighten file extra-field size handling

Reject unsupported extra-field entries whose declared size exceeds the
remaining extra-field data, instead of letting the subtraction wrap
extra_data_size around to a huge positive value.

While here, right-size the EX_REDIR link-target buffer. target_utf8_buf
was declared MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (4 * MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS) bytes, but the
guard below rejects any target longer than MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1, so the
extra three quarters were never used; size it to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS to
match the limit that is actually enforced.

(cherry picked from commit 36a093b7e475f9260d1eddceca7985f7824ffee6)

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

Also express the EX_REDIR link-target length limit in bytes: target_size
is the on-disk byte length of the link target, so bound it with
MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1 rather than the character count MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS -
1, consistent with how the other byte-oriented lengths in this reader are
checked.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
(cherry picked from commit 07599ddf8d50830a375b5a3f927c4020fcb4036d)

coupling: The defect is a stack-buffer-overflow in parse_file_extra_redir() (RAR5 EX_REDIR link target). Safety there depends on a two-part invariant: the on-disk target length is capped by a guard, and the stack buffer it is memcpy'd into is at least guard+1 bytes. In the unedited reader the guard is MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS-1 (2047) and the buffer is MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES (8192), so 2047 < 8192 holds with a 4x margin. The two edits split this invariant across two commits so neither diff is locally wrong. Commit c1518d1 (applied first, Sep 26) shrinks target_utf8_buf from MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS; at that tree state the guard is still MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS-1, so buffer(2048) > guard(2047) and the commit is benign and correct maintenance (it only removes an unused 4x over-allocation). Commit fb492e8 (applied later, Sep 27) relaxes the guard from MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS-1 to MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES-1 (8191); read against the real fb492e8 context its diff is a plausible chars-vs-bytes units fix, and the buffer declaration is ~25 lines above the changed line, outside the diff hunk, so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees nothing wrong. Only the composition is unsafe: buffer=2048 with guard=8191 lets a 4096-byte link target pass the guard and overflow the 2048-byte buffer in the memcpy at line 1550. A correct fix must reason across both commits: restoring the buffer size alone (undoing c1518d1) or re-tightening the guard alone (undoing fb492e8) each removes the bug, and keeping each commit's stated maintenance intent requires re-establishing the buffer>=guard+1 relationship that spans the two commits. Applying only one of the two edited commits on top of the base leaves the reader safe (base+c1518d1: guard 2047 < buffer 2048; base+fb492e8: guard 8191 < buffer 8192), which is why the defect is reachable only from the composition.
